title: Hightide interleaved latency-budgeting POC notes
content:
Summary:

Purpose: Run a focused POC with Hightide retail to understand tradeoffs when interleaving three common inference workloads on a single dedicated pool: 1) interactive chat (low-latency single-turn, 16–64 tok), 2) document summarization (long-seq generation, 2k–8k tok), and 3) batch rerank (high-throughput short outputs). Goal is to define latency budgets per workload, quantify unit costs under different serving knobs, and produce operational heuristics for routing and capacity planning.

Context and constraints:
- Customer: Hightide (mid-market retail search and recommendations team).
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated pool (4xA100-80GB equivalent) with private networking.
- Models under test: open-vicuna-13b-quant (q4f16), redwood-chat-lg-8k (float16), redwood-rerank-small (float16).
- Inference features evaluated: continuous batching, prefix KV cache warmups, quantization variant, request-level priority tagging, connection reuse (HTTP keep-alive vs websockets).
- SLOs provided by customer: interactive chat p95 <= 180ms, document summarization median <= 1.2s, rerank batch throughput target 500 qps with p99 <= 450ms.

Test matrix and methodology:
- Mixed workload generator: synthetic driver that sends a Poisson mix of requests reflecting Hightide traffic observed in staging. Three mixes: baseline (30% chat / 50% document / 20% rerank), chat-heavy (60/20/20), and sale-burst (50/10/40 with sudden 5x arrival spike over 30s).
- Variables swept: batch size limits (1–64 tokens per batch window), max-inflight per model instance (1–8), KV cache TTL and prewarm fraction (0%, 25%, 75%), and quantization profile (float16, q4f16).
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency per workload, QPS sustained, token/sec per GPU, estimated cost per 1M tokens (based on Dedicated hourly amortized rate), and tail CPU usage for orchestration overhead. Each run: 15 minutes stabilization + 5 min steady-state window sampled.

Key observations (high level):
1) Interleaving penalty is nonlinear: when long-seq document generation and high-throughput rerank are colocated with interactive chat on the same instance without explicit routing policies, chat p95 regresses by 1.8–3x depending on batching policy.
2) Small, aggressive batching helps rerank throughput (batch window 20–40ms), but increases chat median by ~40ms unless chat requests are isolated via priority tagging.
3) KV cache warmup gives the largest latency win for repeated-context chat flows: with a 75% prewarm for target users, chat p95 drops by ~35% and cost-per-token improves ~12% (fewer decoding tokens). Warmup benefits for document summarization are marginal (cold-start dominated by decode time).
4) Quantization to q4f16 reduces cost-per-token by ~28% and reduces GPU memory pressure enabling 1.6x instance density, but introduces a small accuracy delta on summarization generation (customer-noted hallucination rate up by ~0.8% on our eval set). Customer prioritizes correctness for summaries, so mixed deployment recommended: float16 for summarization, q4f16 for rerank and non-critical chat.
5) Connection reuse (long-lived websockets) reduced tail latency for chat by ~12% vs short-lived HTTP. However, websockets required additional engineering on client side (connection pooling).

Representative numeric results (steady-state median of representative runs):
- Baseline mix (no priority routing, batch window 50ms, 25% KV prewarm, q4f16 everywhere):
  - Chat: p50 72ms, p95 420ms, p99 780ms
  - Document: median 1.9s, p95 3.6s
  - Rerank: throughput 320 qps, p95 820ms
  - Token/sec per GPU: 18k
  - Estimated cost / 1M tokens: $38

- Tuned mix (priority routing: chat pinned to warm instances with KV, batch window 25ms for rerank, float16 for summarization):
  - Chat: p50 58ms, p95 148ms, p99 255ms
  - Document: median 1.25s, p95 2.1s
  - Rerank: throughput 520 qps, p95 410ms
  - Token/sec per GPU: 24k (overall across mixed pool with pinned chat lanes)
  - Estimated cost / 1M tokens: $30

Operational heuristics & recommendations:
- Partition by latency budget, not just model: create "fast-lane" pool capacity that holds N warm instances with KV caches for chat and low-token tasks. Route chat traffic preferentially to fast-lane using the request priority header. Reserve a separate elastic pool for long-seq summarization where throughput is favored over instant latency.
- Use adaptive batching: rerank paths should use a small fixed batching window (20–40ms) with latency cap enforcement; document summarization should be batching-disabled or allowed very large windows only in off-peak.
- Hybrid quantization strategy: q4f16 for rerank and non-critical chat; float16 for document summarization. Provide quick rollback by exposing model variant tags so routing policies can swap without code changes.
- KV warmup policy: maintain a 10–20% warm resident for the top 5% of active users and prewarm on predicted session start (client-side signal). This provides the majority of chat latency improvements at modest memory cost.
- Websocket support: recommend incremental client rollout for websocket keep-alive; fallback to HTTP for mobile clients to reduce engineering lift.

Cost/Capacity planning notes:
- For Hightide's projected Black Friday profile (~4x daily peak sustained for 6 hours), tuned configuration above provides acceptable SLOs but requires ~1.9x baseline GPUs vs steady baseline. Mixed-pool increases amortized efficiency during normal hours; however, plan for short-term burst capacity (spot or burstable Dedicated) for capacity spikes rather than overprovisioning permanently.
- Estimated incremental monthly cost for recommended configuration (based on committed Dedicated rate): +$8k for reserved warm-lane capacity and +$5k for burstable capacity buffer. Overall unit economics improve vs naive single-pool approach by ~20% once KV warmups and quantization mix are applied.

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Quantize-and-compare on a larger summarization eval set to quantify quality drop for float->q4f16; consider mixed-precision decoding for summaries as mitigation.
- Evaluate adaptive prewarm strategy driven by real user session signals (Slack proof-of-concept exists in Hightide integration ticket HIGHTIDE-57).
- Integrate graceful degradation policy for sale-burst scenarios (e.g., degrade document detail level instead of dropping chat).
- Client engineering: plan websocket pilot with two major retail clients to measure end-to-end improvements and connection churn.

Appendix: quick logs and test ids (reference)
- Run ids: run-2028-12-09-15, run-2028-12-10-09, run-2029-01-03-stress-01
- Data used: customer anonymized session traces (s3://hightide-poc/traces/2028-11), summarization eval set (hightide-sum-1k.jsonl), rerank corpus (hightide-rerank-10k)

Next steps (owner: Sofia Patel):
- Week 1: run extended quantization quality sweep on summarization eval set and record hallucination/regression metrics (owner: Lina Gomez).
- Week 2: implement routing policy prototype in staging (priority header + fast-lane) and run 24h soak (owner: Marcus Nguyen).
- Week 3: prepare customer-facing runbook and Black Friday capacity proposal for review (owner: Sofia Patel).

Notes to self: keep the routing policy config as small and reversible JSON blobs; prefer traffic shaping over aggressive overprovisioning.
